content.value_statement: Large AI projects need clear agent roles, durable memory, and reliable decisions. This skill guides Claude Flow hive minds with queen-led coordination and consensus workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize and spawn Claude Flow hive mind sessions.
Compares strategic, tactical, and adaptive queen coordination modes.
Describes majority, weighted, and Byzantine consensus options.
Shows session management, checkpoint, pause, resume, export, and import workflows.
Documents collective memory storage, retrieval, association, and optimization patterns.
Covers integrations with Claude Code, SPARC workflows, and GitHub review tasks.
limitations: Requires a working Claude Flow installation and compatible project environment.
Provides workflow guidance, not a standalone agent runtime.
Command examples need user review before execution in sensitive repositories.
Performance claims depend on the installed Claude Flow version and workload.

use_cases.title: Plan multi-agent feature delivery
use_cases.description: Break a feature into queen coordination, worker roles, consensus checkpoints, and shared memory tasks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate repository analysis
use_cases.description: Use specialized reviewers to analyze code quality, security, tests, and documentation with a final consensus.

use_cases.title: Run research and architecture studies
use_cases.description: Assign researchers and analysts to compare options, store findings, and produce a supported recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple hive mind
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive-mind-advanced skill to plan a basic Claude Flow hive mind for this objective: [objective]. Include queen type, worker roles, and first status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a consensus method
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a decision that needs review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive-mind-advanced skill to compare majority, weighted, and Byzantine consensus for this decision: [decision]. Recommend one method and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design memory and sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive-mind-advanced skill to design session checkpoints and collective memory entries for this project: [project]. Include retention needs and retrieval patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a full delivery workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination across implementation, testing, and review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive-mind-advanced skill to create a full hive mind plan for [project]. Include queen strategy, worker groups, consensus gates, Claude Code integration, and recovery steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a hive mind for a REST API project.
output_examples.output: The result lists a strategic queen, backend, database, tester, and reviewer workers. It adds weighted consensus for architecture decisions and checkpoints after each milestone.

output_examples.input: Pick a consensus model for release readiness.
output_examples.output: The result recommends Byzantine consensus because release approval needs strong agreement. It explains required votes, fallback review, and memory records.

output_examples.input: Create a memory strategy for a long research task.
output_examples.output: The result separates permanent knowledge, session context, task notes, and metrics. It defines when to store, search, associate, and prune records.

best_practices: Select queen type from the task goal before choosing worker roles.
Use stronger consensus for architecture, security, release, and data decisions.
Store reusable findings in collective memory with clear names and confidence levels.
anti_patterns: Do not spawn many workers before defining the objective and decision rules.
Do not use consensus for simple status checks or low-risk routine tasks.
Do not run command examples in production repositories without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate Claude Flow hive mind workflows with queen agents, worker agents, consensus, sessions, and shared memory.

faq.question: Does it run the hive mind automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples for Claude Flow workflows. Users decide what commands to run.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use Byzantine consensus?
faq.answer: Use it for important decisions that need strong agreement, such as architecture, security, release readiness, or compliance choices.

faq.question: What project setup is required?
faq.answer: You need Claude Flow available in the project environment and permission to run related CLI commands.

faq.question: Can it help with code reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes reviewer workers, security review roles, performance review roles, test analysis, and consensus on requested changes.
